actions.verb_sequence: finishes initial logic test writing 'Estimate: 62nd Percentile' over a 12th-percentile paper -> studies the 10-minute logic training packet -> flips back, spots five obvious logic errors, and revises estimate down to a realistic 32%
traces how learning the rule switched the student's internal error-detector ON

reactions.reaction: nods with genuine 'aha!' humility seeing the missed counterexamples
points to the top quartile's small dip (74% vs 87%), noting experts simply assumed peers aced it too

scenes.wardrobe: 1999 Ivy League attire: tweed sport coat and collared shirt on Dunning; crew-neck wool sweater on Kruger; late-1990s fleece vest and flannel shirt on student.

scenes.recognition_hook: Forget the fake internet 'Mount Stupid' cartoon — in Cornell's real 1999 lab, 12th-percentile scorers guessed 62nd, and ten minutes of logic training dropped their overconfidence by teaching them how to see mistakes.

key_visual.description: two 1999 Cornell psychologists beside the real two-line 12%-vs-62% chalkboard graph while a student uses a 10-minute logic packet to spot errors and lower an inflated self-rating
